line: Jung's statements on the syzygy: the pairing of anima and animus, and the paired opposites in which God unfolds in the Gnostic accounts.

sections.title: Anima and animus as a pair
sections.line: CW9ii ¶422 and CW9i ¶145: the syzygy that analysis of the shadow uncovers.

quotes.quote: Through analysis of the shadow and of the processes contained in it we uncover the ANIMA/ANIMUS syzygy.
These show that syzygies were projected which were in complete contradiction to the traditional beliefs, and that they were often experienced in the form of a vision.

sections.title: Paired opposites
sections.line: CW9ii ¶300 and ¶345 and CW14 ¶ 118: the syzygy in the doctrine of the pairs.

quotes.quote: The unknown author understands good and evil as the right and left hand of God, and views the whole of creation in terms of syzygies, or pairs of opposites.
God unfolds himself in the world in the form of syzygies (paired opposites), such as heaven/earth, day/night, male/female, etc.
All three indicate the essential similarity of the components of the syzygy and their “spiritual” nature.
